input.summary: Fixed the one reported finding. The closing sentence of the flexible-pulling-element section no longer asserts that the vibration coupling is invariant to how, how hard, or from what angle the operator pulls; it now states that the coupling is set by the air-extraction mechanism 20 and supplied independently of the tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46, which is what the disclosure supports. Nothing else changed: the claims, the numeral table, the Brief Description of the Drawings and all five figure briefs stand as they were, and I confirmed no similar angle-of-pull wording appears anywhere else in draft/ or figures/.
reasoning: The finding is confined to one sentence in the detailed description, and the reviewer supplied replacement wording that keeps the supported part of the thought. I used it verbatim rather than paraphrasing, since the surrounding sentences in that paragraph were traced and needed to keep their terms.

The removed clause claimed a result the disclosure never states, that coupling quality is unaffected by the direction of the applied tension. The disclosure says the operator controls position with minimal pulling force while the vacuum maintains consistent coupling; it does not say the holding function is indifferent to pull angle, and an upward-inclined pull would work against the holding force. The replacement asserts only independence from the tension, which is the disclosed decoupling.

I checked whether the same over-reach had propagated. The Summary states decoupled control as position set by a small pulling force and the holding force set independently and constantly by the pressure differential, with no angle assertion, so it needed no edit. A search for the removed phrasing across draft/ and figures/ returned nothing further.

No claim recites pull angle or direction, so claim scope is untouched: claim 9, claim 10 and claim 16 recite the pulling element and, in claim 10, that the holding force is supplied independently of the flexible pulling element by the pressure differential. That whereby clause remains fully supported by the amended description.

I verified the earlier repairs survived this cycle rather than assuming it: the description still says the second side 16 is opposite the first side 14, the Brief Description of FIG. 5 still recites the flexible pulling element and its connection as shown schematically, and the five figure briefs are unchanged from the drawing repair, at 2789, 2792, 2031, 2792 and 2765 characters with the explicit hatch directions and the broadened endpoint targets intact.
changes: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section 'Embodiment with a flexible pulling element': the final sentence now reads that the quality of the vibration coupling is set by the air-extraction mechanism 20 and is supplied independently of the tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46, replacing the assertion that it does not vary with how, how hard, or from what angle the operator pulls.
input.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged. Claim 1 continues to rest on the combination no reference in prior_art/ discloses: a rigid low-friction perimeter member that deliberately does not seal, leaving a clearance along at least part of its length through which ambient air enters continuously; an extraction rate sufficient to keep the chamber below atmospheric pressure against that continuous ingress; an all-rigid transmission path from motor to bearing face with no elastomeric member, foam member or resilient mount interposed; and a bearing face slidable over the exposed face while the differential is maintained. The rigid, seal-free perimeter carries the claim clear of US-11408462-B2 and DE-202021002652-U1, which both place a compliant member, elastic partitions or a rubber-elastic apron, in the load path. Simultaneous holding and sliding under one continuously running extraction carries it clear of US-10001245-B2, which surrenders the vacuum and floats on an air cushion to move. The non-sealing clearance, and vibration delivered into the covering element as the working output rather than spent loosening the hold, carry it clear of US-4934475-A. US-11247858-B2 is addressed in the Background for the teaching it actually contains, lifting sheet articles on a perforated suction plate and sweeping debris by suction, and why that does not bear on holding a vibrating tool down on a laid covering element. The amended sentence narrows an explanatory statement in the description and does not touch any distinguishing feature.

The claim that coupling quality is unaffected by how, how hard, or from what angle the operator pulls is gone, and what remains is the disclosed decoupling: position set by a small pulling force, holding force and coupling supplied independently and continuously by the pressure differential. I checked the Summary and the rest of the application for the same over-reach and found none, so no other section needed amending. structured_output.summary: Fixed the one reported finding. The closing sentence of the flexible-pulling-element section no longer asserts that the vibration coupling is invariant to how, how hard, or from what angle the operator pulls; it now states that the coupling is set by the air-extraction mechanism 20 and supplied independently of the tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46, which is what the disclosure supports. Nothing else changed: the claims, the numeral table, the Brief Description of the Drawings and all five figure briefs stand as they were, and I confirmed no similar angle-of-pull wording appears anywhere else in draft/ or figures/.
reasoning: The finding is confined to one sentence in the detailed description, and the reviewer supplied replacement wording that keeps the supported part of the thought. I used it verbatim rather than paraphrasing, since the surrounding sentences in that paragraph were traced and needed to keep their terms.

The removed clause claimed a result the disclosure never states, that coupling quality is unaffected by the direction of the applied tension. The disclosure says the operator controls position with minimal pulling force while the vacuum maintains consistent coupling; it does not say the holding function is indifferent to pull angle, and an upward-inclined pull would work against the holding force. The replacement asserts only independence from the tension, which is the disclosed decoupling.

I checked whether the same over-reach had propagated. The Summary states decoupled control as position set by a small pulling force and the holding force set independently and constantly by the pressure differential, with no angle assertion, so it needed no edit. A search for the removed phrasing across draft/ and figures/ returned nothing further.

No claim recites pull angle or direction, so claim scope is untouched: claim 9, claim 10 and claim 16 recite the pulling element and, in claim 10, that the holding force is supplied independently of the flexible pulling element by the pressure differential. That whereby clause remains fully supported by the amended description.

I verified the earlier repairs survived this cycle rather than assuming it: the description still says the second side 16 is opposite the first side 14, the Brief Description of FIG. 5 still recites the flexible pulling element and its connection as shown schematically, and the five figure briefs are unchanged from the drawing repair, at 2789, 2792, 2031, 2792 and 2765 characters with the explicit hatch directions and the broadened endpoint targets intact.
changes: draft/08-detailed-description.md, section 'Embodiment with a flexible pulling element': the final sentence now reads that the quality of the vibration coupling is set by the air-extraction mechanism 20 and is supplied independently of the tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46, replacing the assertion that it does not vary with how, how hard, or from what angle the operator pulls.
structured_output.prior_art_strategy: Unchanged. Claim 1 continues to rest on the combination no reference in prior_art/ discloses: a rigid low-friction perimeter member that deliberately does not seal, leaving a clearance along at least part of its length through which ambient air enters continuously; an extraction rate sufficient to keep the chamber below atmospheric pressure against that continuous ingress; an all-rigid transmission path from motor to bearing face with no elastomeric member, foam member or resilient mount interposed; and a bearing face slidable over the exposed face while the differential is maintained. The rigid, seal-free perimeter carries the claim clear of US-11408462-B2 and DE-202021002652-U1, which both place a compliant member, elastic partitions or a rubber-elastic apron, in the load path. Simultaneous holding and sliding under one continuously running extraction carries it clear of US-10001245-B2, which surrenders the vacuum and floats on an air cushion to move. The non-sealing clearance, and vibration delivered into the covering element as the working output rather than spent loosening the hold, carry it clear of US-4934475-A. US-11247858-B2 is addressed in the Background for the teaching it actually contains, lifting sheet articles on a perforated suction plate and sweeping debris by suction, and why that does not bear on holding a vibrating tool down on a laid covering element. The amended sentence narrows an explanatory statement in the description and does not touch any distinguishing feature.
structured_output.answer: The decoupled-control paragraph now ends: 'Position is thus controlled by one agency and contact by another: the operator sets where the vibration device 10 is with a small pulling force, while the quality of the vibration coupling is set by the air-extraction mechanism 20 and is supplied independently of the tension applied to the flexible pulling element 46.' The claim that coupling quality is unaffected by how, how hard, or from what angle the operator pulls is gone, and what remains is the disclosed decoupling: position set by a small pulling force, holding force and coupling supplied independently and continuously by the pressure differential. I checked the Summary and the rest of the application for the same over-reach and found none, so no other section needed amending. The claims were unaffected, since none recites pull angle or direction, and claim 10's whereby clause, which recites the holding force being supplied independently of the flexible pulling element by the pressure differential, remains supported by the amended text. The numeral table, the Brief Description of the Drawings and all five figure briefs are untouched, and I confirmed the previous repairs are still in place, including the schematic recital for the pulling element and its connection in the FIG. 5 sentence, the explicit hatch directions on the two sectional sheets, and the broadened endpoint targets for numerals 24 and 36.
